outcome: The Lang-Trotter conjecture on supersingular primes for a non-CM elliptic curve over Q (that the count of supersingular primes below X is asymptotically c*sqrt(X)/log(X)) remains open; no proof, disproof, or case-settling result on the stated problem itself was found in the window.
summary: The stated problem is Lang and Trotter's 1976 conjecture that for a non-CM elliptic curve E over Q, the number of primes p < X at which E has supersingular reduction is asymptotically c_E * sqrt(X)/log(X) for a constant c_E depending on E. Searches (WebSearch for 'Lang-Trotter conjecture supersingular primes 2024 2025 proof', 'Lang-Trotter conjecture supersingular primes arXiv', and 'Lang-Trotter conjecture AI machine learning neural network elliptic curve') turned up a cluster of arXiv papers dated 2024-2026, but every one addresses a different or narrower object than the stated conjecture: 'Distribution of supersingular primes for abelian surfaces' (arXiv:2402.12218, submitted 19 Feb 2024, revised 9 Jul 2025) and 'On distribution of supersingular primes of abelian varieties and K3 surfaces' (arXiv:2504.08088) both move to abelian surfaces/K3 surfaces, not elliptic curves; 'The Lang-Trotter conjecture on average for genus-2 curves with Klein-4 reduced automorphism group' (arXiv:2408.13695) and the analogous S3 paper (arXiv:2604.00822) are genus-2 average results, a different object and a weaker (on-average) statement; the CM elliptic curve paper (arXiv:2109.14256, pre-window) and the y^2=x^3+Dx family paper (arXiv:2108.06292, pre-window) both predate the window and additionally concern the CM case, which is a different hypothesis than the non-CM case stated in the conjecture. I opened arXiv:2402.12218 directly (via WebFetch) and confirmed it studies abelian surfaces, not elliptic curves, and contains no proof or disproof of the classical conjecture, and no mention of AI/ML tool use. I also fetched the current (2026) Wikipedia article on supersingular primes for elliptic curves, which explicitly states 'As of 2026, this conjecture remains open' and cites no new result since Cojocaru-Fouvry-Murty 2005. A separate search for AI/ML connections turned up only an unrelated paper ('Learning Euler Factors of Elliptic Curves', arXiv:2502.10357) on predicting Euler factors/murmurations via machine learning, which does not touch the supersingular-prime-counting conjecture at all. No case of the stated conjecture (e.g., a specific non-CM curve or family proved to match the asymptotic exactly, or the asymptotic constant pinned down) was found settled, and no bound on the counting function was found to have moved. This matches the triage's 'none' verdict. Status is open with no_change_found true, and ai_role is none.
competing_reading: One could argue the genus-2 'Lang-Trotter on average' papers are extensions that constitute 'progress on the Lang-Trotter program' broadly, but per the scope rule (§3.1) they change the object (elliptic curve -> genus-2 curve/abelian surface) and the statement (asymptotic -> on-average asymptotic), which makes them related problems rather than cases of the stated conjecture (restricting to a sub-case of the same object and same statement). None of them settle any sub-case of the non-CM elliptic curve conjecture itself.
what_would_settle_it: A paper proving the asymptotic c_E*sqrt(X)/log(X) (or even just establishing existence of a positive-density/exact-order lower and upper bound matching this rate) for a specific non-CM elliptic curve E over Q, or for an infinite non-trivial subfamily of non-CM curves, would count as partial progress on the stated problem; currently the best known results are Elkies' infinitude of supersingular primes and Fouvry-Murty/Cojocaru-type average results, none of which pin down the exact asymptotic order for any individual non-CM curve.
